_about: Bible edition registry. 'bundled' editions are generated into public/data/bible by `npm run data:build`. 'planned' editions are listed so the UI can explain, honestly, why they are not available: they are under copyright and need a license or a publisher API.

bundled.name: Douay-Rheims Bible (Challoner revision, 1899 American edition)
bundled.tradition: Translated from the Latin Vulgate (Clementine). Vulgate chapter, verse and Psalm numbering.
bundled.description: The traditional Catholic English Bible, translated from the Latin Vulgate at Douay and Rheims (1582–1610) and revised by Bishop Richard Challoner (1749–52). The 1899 American edition. It follows the Vulgate numbering, so Psalms 9–147 are numbered one lower than in most modern Bibles; the reader shows both numbers. Archaic vocabulary and spellings of names (Isaias, Osee, Josue) are the translators' own.
bundled.translators: English College at Douai; revised by Richard Challoner
bundled.catholicStatus: A historic Catholic English translation of the Vulgate. Not the current liturgical Lectionary text.
bundled.rightsBasis: Published 1899 (translators died centuries ago). eBible.org distributes it as Public Domain.
bundled.attribution: Douay-Rheims 1899 American Edition, text from eBible.org (public domain).
bundled.offByDefault: The Douay-Rheims is a treasured Catholic translation, but its English is from the 1500s–1700s: “thee”, “saith”, “Isaias”, “Osee”, long sentences and older word meanings. Most readers find modern English easier, and it numbers the Psalms differently from most Bibles (Psalm 23 appears as Psalm 22). It is still in the app because many of the Fathers and the Haydock and Challoner notes are written against it.
bundled.approvalNote: The Challoner revision of the Douay-Rheims was the standard Catholic Bible in English for about two centuries, used with the approval of the Church’s bishops.

bundled.name: Clementine Vulgate (Sixto-Clementine, 1598)
bundled.tradition: Latin Vulgate (St. Jerome and later hands), Sixto-Clementine text. Psalms are the Gallican Psalter.
bundled.description: The Latin text of the Sixto-Clementine Vulgate, the Church's standard Latin Bible until the Nova Vulgata (1979) and the text the Douay-Rheims translates. This edition is anchored to the Vulgate numbering; every other edition is mapped to it. The same file also carries the Glossa Ordinaria (Migne, 1880) as verse-level footnotes, which the app shows as historical commentary.
bundled.translators: St. Jerome (and others); edited under Popes Sixtus V and Clement VIII
bundled.catholicStatus: The historic Latin Vulgate of the Roman Church (superseded by the Nova Vulgata for liturgical use).
bundled.rightsBasis: Published 1598 / 1880. eBible.org distributes it as Public Domain.
bundled.attribution: Clementine Vulgate with Glossa Ordinaria (Migne 1880), text from eBible.org (public domain).
bundled.offByDefault: This is the Latin Vulgate, not English. It is here for study and comparison (the Glossa Ordinaria notes belong to it), and it is not meant as a first reading text. Its Psalm numbering also differs from most Bibles.
bundled.approvalNote: The Clementine Vulgate was the Church’s official Latin Bible for centuries (until the Nova Vulgata of 1979).

bundled.name: World English Bible, Catholic edition
bundled.tradition: Modern English. Protocanonical books from the Hebrew and Greek; deuterocanonical books and the additions to Esther and Daniel from the Greek (Septuagint / Theodotion). English-tradition numbering.
bundled.description: A modern, public-domain English translation arranged in the Catholic book order with the deuterocanon. It is included as a plain-English reading aid next to the Douay-Rheims. It is NOT an ecclesiastically approved Catholic translation. Because Tobit, Judith, Sirach, Esther and Daniel follow the Greek texts rather than the Vulgate, their chapters and verses do not line up with the Douay-Rheims and the app says so wherever it matters.
bundled.catholicStatus: Not an approved Catholic translation; included as a public-domain modern-English reading aid with the Catholic canon.
bundled.rightsBasis: Dedicated to the public domain by its translators. 'World English Bible' is a trademark of eBible.org: the text must not be altered and still called WEB. The app changes only formatting, never wording.
bundled.attribution: World English Bible (Catholic), from eBible.org (public domain).
bundled.approvalNote: Not a Church-approved translation: a modern public-domain translation arranged with the Catholic canon.

bundled.name: Catholic Public Domain Version (CPDV)
bundled.tradition: Translated from the Latin Vulgate in plain modern English; Vulgate (Douay) chapter, verse and Psalm numbering.
bundled.description: A recent Catholic translation of the Latin Vulgate into straightforward modern English, made by Ronald L. Conte Jr. and placed in the public domain. It follows the same numbering as the Douay-Rheims (Psalms 9–147 are numbered one lower than in most modern Bibles; the reader shows both) but without the archaic vocabulary.
bundled.catholicStatus: A privately made Catholic translation of the Vulgate. It has no imprimatur and is not the Lectionary text.
bundled.rightsBasis: Dedicated to the public domain by its translator (see sacredbible.org/catholic). Text taken from the scrollmapper/bible_databases JSON export.
bundled.attribution: Catholic Public Domain Version, Ronald L. Conte Jr. (public domain).
bundled.approvalNote: Not Church-approved: a privately made Catholic translation of the Vulgate, with no imprimatur.

bundled.name: The Septuagint in English (Brenton, 1851)
bundled.tradition: Translated from the Greek Septuagint, the ancient Greek Old Testament the early Church read. Psalm numbering follows the Septuagint, which is the Vulgate (Douay) numbering. The Old Testament and deuterocanon only; there is no New Testament.
bundled.description: Sir Lancelot Brenton's 1851 English translation of the Septuagint (the Greek Old Testament used by the apostles and the Fathers), lightly modernised in spelling by eBible.org. Useful beside the Douay-Rheims for seeing what the Greek reads where it differs from the Hebrew. Only books whose chapter numbering lines up with the Vulgate are included (so Jeremiah, Esther, Daniel, Tobit, Judith, Sirach and a few others are left out). In the books that are included, a few chapters number their verses one or two differently from the Douay-Rheims, so a verse here can sit a verse away from the same verse elsewhere.
bundled.catholicStatus: A Protestant (Anglican) 19th-century translation of the Greek Old Testament. It is not a Church-approved translation, but the Septuagint it translates is the Old Testament text the early Church used.
bundled.rightsBasis: Published in 1851; eBible.org's edition is stated to be in the public domain (https://ebible.org/eng-Brenton/copyright.htm).
bundled.attribution: Septuagint, translated by Sir Lancelot C. L. Brenton (1851), public domain, text from eBible.org.
bundled.offByDefault: The Septuagint is the Greek Old Testament, not a translation of the Vulgate. Its English is from 1851 and its Old Testament books can differ in wording, order and length from the Hebrew-based and Latin-based Bibles. It is offered for comparison, not as a Church-approved reading Bible.
bundled.approvalNote: A private 19th-century Protestant translation of the Septuagint; not Church-approved. The Septuagint itself is the Greek Old Testament of the early Church.

bundled.name: Revised Standard Version, Second Catholic Edition (The Ignatius Bible)
bundled.tradition: A literal English translation in the Tyndale–King James tradition, from the Hebrew, Aramaic and Greek, with the Catholic deuterocanonical books. English-tradition numbering; Psalms use the Hebrew numbering (the Greek/Vulgate number is shown by the reader).
bundled.description: The Revised Standard Version, Second Catholic Edition, as published by Ignatius Press (title page: ‘revised according to Liturgiam Authenticam, 2002’). A formal-equivalence translation widely used in Catholic study and prayer. Read this before relying on it: the text here was read from a scan of the printed book, not from a publisher file. The scan garbles most printed verse numbers, so chapter and verse breaks were rebuilt automatically. About 6 in 10 verse starts rest on a legible printed number; the rest were placed by matching the wording to a reference text, so now and then a clause can sit in the neighbouring verse, and a stray scan mark can remain. Esther and Zechariah are left out until their text can be checked. The book’s footnotes and cross-references are not included.
bundled.translators: National Council of the Churches of Christ in the USA; Catholic edition prepared by the Catholic Biblical Association of Great Britain; Second Catholic Edition revised by Ignatius Press
bundled.catholicStatus: A Catholic edition of the RSV, revised according to Liturgiam Authenticam, published by Ignatius Press. The scan used here has no imprimatur page, so this app does not state who approved it; check your own copy. Not the Lectionary text.
bundled.rightsBasis: © National Council of the Churches of Christ in the USA / Ignatius Press. Included with the project owner’s statement (Nov 2026) that permission to use it has been obtained; the licence reference is to be recorded in docs/LICENSING.md. Remove the pack if that permission lapses.
bundled.attribution: The Holy Bible, Revised Standard Version, Second Catholic Edition (Ignatius Bible), © Ignatius Press / NCC USA, used with permission. Text read from a scan; verse breaks rebuilt automatically.

bundled.name: New American Bible, Revised Edition (NABRE)
bundled.tradition: A modern English translation made from the Hebrew, Aramaic and Greek by Catholic scholars for the United States bishops. Hebrew-based verse numbering: the Psalm titles count as verses and a few chapters (Joel, Malachi and some others) divide differently from the English-tradition Bibles.
bundled.description: The New American Bible, Revised Edition: the New Testament of 1986, the Psalms of 1991 and the Old Testament revised in 2010, as published by Saint Benedict Press with the Church’s approval for Catholic use. This pack carries the translation text with its book and section headings. The footnotes, cross-references and book introductions of the printed edition are not included here, and neither are the lettered Greek additions to Esther (A–F) or the foreword to Sirach, so a few passages in those books are not shown; read them in a printed copy or on the USCCB site. Where the printed text places a verse at the start or end of the neighbouring chapter (for example Job 10:1, Numbers 25:19 or Tobit 6:1), the pack puts it where its number says it belongs.
bundled.translators: Confraternity of Christian Doctrine; Catholic Biblical Association of America and other scholars, for the United States Conference of Catholic Bishops
bundled.catholicStatus: Translated from the original languages and approved by the Administrative Committee of the United States Conference of Catholic Bishops, with the imprimaturs printed in the edition (New Testament 1986, Psalms 1991, Old Testament rescript of 30 September 2010). It is the base text of the U.S. lectionary tradition but is not itself the current Lectionary for Mass.
bundled.rightsBasis: © 2008, 1991, 1986, 1970 Confraternity of Christian Doctrine, Inc., Washington, DC. All rights reserved. Included with the project owner’s statement (Nov 2026) that official permission to include the NABRE has been obtained; the permission reference is to be recorded in docs/LICENSING.md. Remove the pack if that permission lapses.
bundled.attribution: Scripture texts are taken from the New American Bible, revised edition © 2008, 1991, 1986, 1970 Confraternity of Christian Doctrine, Inc., Washington, DC. All rights reserved. Used with permission.
bundled.approvalNote: Approved for Catholic use by the United States Conference of Catholic Bishops (imprimaturs printed in the edition). Not the Lectionary text.

planned.name: Revised Standard Version, Catholic Edition (RSV-CE)
planned.publisher: Ignatius Press / National Council of the Churches of Christ in the USA
planned.note: Under copyright. Requires a license from the rights holders (and a Bible-publisher agreement for app use). The app's edition format, anchor mapping and licensing records are ready to receive it; the mapping from English numbering is already implemented.

planned.name: New Jerusalem Bible / Jerusalem Bible
planned.note: Under copyright. Requires a license from the publisher.

planned.name: Other editions via a licensed Bible API (e.g. API.Bible)
planned.publisher: American Bible Society and content partners
planned.note: A pluggable provider interface exists for fetching licensed text with your own API key at read time. Requires credentials and per-edition terms; not enabled in this build.
